title: Pod capacity morning scrapbook
content:
Morning quicknotes (scratchpad) - pod capacity + networking focus.

Top-of-mind items:
- Weird tail latencies on hosted edge-region-3 between 03:20-03:40 UTC yesterday. p95 jumped ~120ms for short chat requests. Possible small eviction storms?
- NVLink errors on pod-rtx-11: dmesg shows repeated timeout followed by reset. Need to capture before rebooting.
- Prefill cache miss spike correlates with new canary consumer (canary-app-7) ramping up. Investigate routing rules.

Immediate TODOs (priority order):
[ ] Confirm whether pod-rtx-11 ECC scrub ran overnight (check /var/log/nvme and gpu-manager logs).
[ ] Run `kubectl describe pod pod-rtx-11 -n rdedicated` and save events to /tmp/pod-rtx-11-events-$(date +%F).log
[ ] Collect kernel ring buffer: `sudo journalctl -k -u gpu-drivers.service --since "2026-03-12 00:00" > ~/logs/gpu-klog-0312.txt`
[ ] Throttle canary-app-7 to 20qps via routing policy rollback; leave note in #gpu-ops.
[ ] Check autoscaler scale-down policy: did scale-down coincide with the p95 spike? Review metrics in Console > Dedicated > clusters/edge-3 > autoscaler (last 48h).
[ ] If capacity < target, open JIRA PLAT-4182 with capacity delta + recommended hotfix (temp bump reserved count).

Short diagnostic checklist:
- GPU health: `rd-inferctl nodes ls --region edge-3 --fields name,gpu_health,mem_free` (target mem_free > 20GB on each node for current workload).
- NVLink: `nvidia-smi nvlink --status` output + `dmesg | grep -i nvlink`
- Disk: `iostat -x 1 5` on pods showing high iowait (especially embedding workers).
- Network: check flow logs for pod namespace (vpc-flow capture) for drops or SYN retries during spike window.

Notes/observations:
- Yesterday we merged infra PR to increase batch_size for small-chat route (PR #389). That increases per-token GPU work slightly — could explain p95 shift on small requests. Keep an eye on cost delta.
- Cache warming: there is an in-progress warmup job for top-200 prompts (ticket PLAT-4129). If warmup runs while autoscaler scaling-to-zero occurs, we may see transient misses. Consider adding sticky-min replicas for warmup window.
- BPF programs on host have a high filter count; SRE mentioned a kernel upgrade last week that changed BPF memory defaults. Could cause longer attach times for new flows. File: notes/kernel-bpf-change-2026-03-05 in shared drive (link pinned in Slack).

Commands I ran this morning (save for runbook entry):
- `kubectl get hpa -n rdedicated | grep edge-3` -> HPA looked healthy (cpu 42%)
- `rd-inferctl metrics query --metric p95_latency --service small-chat --from 2026-03-12T02:30Z --to 2026-03-12T04:30Z --group-by node` -> node-level p95 shows spike on nodes node-rtx-11 & node-rtx-12
- `ssh rtx-11` -> `sudo systemctl status gpu-drivers` -> intermittent restart logged at 03:27 UTC

Questions to follow up with folks:
- @Liam Chen: did the canary team change concurrency settings or retry policy for canary-app-7 yesterday morning? (I saw a retention bump in the canary config but need confirmation.)
- @Noah Rivera: can SRE pull full host kernel logs for node-rtx-11 for 03:00-04:00 UTC (including early-boot messages)? I want to correlate NVLink timeouts with any kernel watchdogs.
- @product-hosted-api team: is the small-chat batch_size increase still required? If not, revert PR #389 to measure delta.

Quick ideas / hypothesis (brain dump):
- Hypothesis A: a combination of short-lived autoscaler scale-downs + cache warmup + a slight batch_size increase created queueing at the model server for small chats, pushing p95 up.
- Hypothesis B: underlying host driver instability (NVLink timeouts) causes a small fraction of tokens to be retried, creating tail spikes.

Follow-ups to log into runbook and ticket:
- Add steps to runbook for NVLink transient: capture nvidia-smi logs, save kernel dumps, optional reboot procedure.
- Add a remediation play for warmup+scaling collisions: enforce min-replicas during scheduled warmup windows.

Random todo (low priority):
- Clean up old logs under ~/logs/* (older than 14d) on jumpbox.
- Revisit cost estimate for batch_size change Feb->Mar. Put notes into shared_drives/engineering/optimize/costs/batch-size-impact.md

End of morning scratchpad. Will convert critical steps to tickets after confirming NVLink repeats on next 2 checks.

-- Asha
summary: Personal morning ops scratchpad focused on pod capacity, NVLink errors, cache warmup, and quick diagnostics. Contains immediate TODOs, commands run, hypotheses, and follow-ups to convert to tickets.
